title: feat: add Windows support for connect, start, pause, and resume
body:
Adds Windows support for connect, start, pause, and resume.

- Credentials: stored in Windows Credential Manager via CredWrite, with the secret passed over stdin (no cmdkey, so the token never appears in a command line or process list).
- Background sync: uses a Scheduled Task named dev.cribble.agent.sync.
- Darwin behavior is unchanged: Keychain and LaunchAgent paths are untouched.
- On Windows, ccusage is resolved to its JS bin and run through node directly, rather than relying on npm .bin shims.
- Collection, HTTP, and payload behavior are otherwise unchanged.

title: feat: add Linux support for connect, start, pause, and resume
body:
Adds Linux support for connect, start, pause, and resume.

- Credentials: stored in the Secret Service keyring via libsecret's `secret-tool`, with the secret passed over stdin so the token never appears in a command line or process list. A missing item (exit 1, empty stderr) is distinguished from an unreachable keyring, which gets actionable guidance pointing headless machines at `CRIBBLE_API_KEY`.
- Background sync: systemd user units `dev.cribble.agent.sync.service` + `.timer` under `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/systemd/user`, with the same on-the-hour interval semantics as the LaunchAgent and the same install/pause/resume/uninstall rollback discipline. The kickstart uses `start --no-block` to queue the oneshot sync like `launchctl kickstart`.
- Darwin behavior is unchanged: Keychain and LaunchAgent paths are untouched. The platform dispatch deliberately mirrors the structure of the Windows port in #3 (`requireSupportedPlatform`, per-platform implementations behind the public functions), so whichever PR lands second should rebase easily.
- Status and CLI messages name the platform credential store instead of always saying macOS Keychain; previously Linux `status` misreported the missing key as an "unreadable macOS Keychain key".
- Collection, HTTP, and payload behavior are otherwise unchanged (`cribble show`/`sync` already worked on Linux via ccusage).

Validation:
- 92 unit tests pass (13 new Linux cases, fake-spawn based so they run on any platform).
- `scripts/linux-live-test.sh` (included) runs the real lifecycle end to end inside a disposable systemd Docker container with an unlocked GNOME Keyring: connect stores the key, `start` arms the timer on the correct calendar marks, and the kickstarted background sync reads the key from the keyring inside a systemd user service (no explicit DBus address — libsecret resolves the bus from `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR`) before stopping at the no-usage-data error, so the test key never reaches the network. Pause, resume, uninstall, and disconnect are asserted against real `systemctl --user` and `secret-tool` state.
- CI gains an ubuntu smoke job asserting the credential and background APIs either answer or fail with their actionable guidance on runners without an unlocked keyring or user bus.

title: Make ccusage collection window-aware for large histories
body:
## Problem

`cribble-agent` terminates unified ccusage collection after 60 seconds. On machines with a large local history, ccusage can complete successfully just beyond that boundary, while `cribble` reports only `Could not read ccusage data.`

Current source:

- `lib/source.js` invokes bundled `ccusage daily --json`
- child timeout is fixed at `60_000`
- the requested `--days` value is applied only after the full ccusage report has been collected

Reproduction on Linux with `cribble-agent@1.3.0` / `ccusage@20.0.20`:

```text
cribble --json
→ Cribble error: Could not read ccusage data.

same bundled ccusage command
→ exit 0 in 65.750 seconds
```

The same command under `loadUsage()` is terminated with `ETIMEDOUT` / `SIGTERM` at 60 seconds.

## Proposed behavior

- Make collection time-bounded without imposing a brittle fixed ceiling on valid histories.
- Pass the requested date window into ccusage (`--since` or an equivalent supported filter) before parsing, so `cribble --days 7` does not require scanning all history.
- Retain a bounded configurable ceiling with a clear timeout error that identifies ccusage collection as the failing stage.
- Keep scheduled and foreground behavior consistent.

## Acceptance

- A fixture collector that completes after the old 60-second boundary succeeds within the new configured policy.
- `--days N` constrains source collection, not only post-collection slicing.
- A genuinely hung collector is still terminated.
- Timeout errors report the configured duration and actionable remediation.
- Existing source-environment scrubbing and output-size bounds remain intact.

This issue was prepared with AI assistance and verified against the installed 1.3.0 package and bundled ccusage 20.0.20.

title: Preserve HERMES_HOME for unified ccusage collection
body:
## Problem

Cribble invokes ccusage with an explicit environment allowlist. It preserves `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` and `CODEX_HOME`, but drops `HERMES_HOME`.

ccusage supports Hermes Agent and accepts multiple comma-separated Hermes roots. Hermes named profiles keep independent `state.db` files, so removing an explicit `HERMES_HOME` can make foreground and scheduled Cribble reports miss profile usage.

Current source:

```js
const COLLECTOR_ENV_KEYS = [
  // ...
  "CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR",
  "CODEX_HOME",
  // HERMES_HOME absent
]
```

The local sanitized child environment confirmed `HERMES_HOME` is absent.

## Proposed behavior

- Preserve an explicit non-empty `HERMES_HOME` when launching ccusage.
- Document that multiple roots use ccusage's existing delimiter contract.
- Keep the allowlist fail-closed: do not pass unrelated credentials or provider keys.
- Ensure background install/repair captures the same explicit value as foreground sync.

A later convenience improvement could discover default and named profile roots when the variable is absent, but explicit configuration should work first.

## Acceptance

- Explicit single-root and multi-root `HERMES_HOME` reach the ccusage child unchanged.
- Empty/unset values remain absent.
- unrelated environment secrets remain excluded.
- foreground and scheduled-service paths use the same value.
- tests cover aliases/deduplication, unreadable stores, symlink escapes, and delimiter-invalid paths if automatic discovery is added.

Related prior art: tokenmaxxing PR #68 handles named Hermes profiles across initial service install and repair while preserving explicit configuration.

This issue was prepared with AI assistance and verified against `cribble-agent@1.3.0` and current ccusage Hermes support.

title: fix: write WorkingDirectory= literally so Linux background sync can start
body:
Every `cribble start` on Linux currently fails with "Installing Linux background sync failed: ... Job failed."

systemd path settings such as `WorkingDirectory=` take their value literally — quotes are not parsed there — so the quoted path is rejected as "not absolute" and the service unit becomes fatally invalid, which makes the timer refuse to start.

- `WorkingDirectory=` is now written literally with only `%` specifier escaping. `ExecStart=` keeps `systemdQuote` (quotes are valid command-line syntax there).
- Rollback, pause, and uninstall no longer treat "Unit not loaded" from `systemctl stop`/`disable` as a failure: cleaning up a unit systemd never loaded is a successful cleanup, and reporting it as "Rollback also failed" buried the actionable install error. This also lets `cribble background uninstall` recover installs left with a fatally invalid unit by 1.4.0-beta.1.

Verified in a disposable systemd container (real `systemctl --user` and GNOME Keyring): connect, start, timer scheduling, a kickstarted sync that reads the key from the keyring, pause, resume, and uninstall. Regression tests pin the unit format and the rollback behavior.

title: fix: release stdin after the hidden key prompt so connect can exit
body:
After a successful `cribble connect`, the CLI hangs in interactive terminals until Ctrl+C. This affects all platforms and predates 1.4 — piped input masks it because EOF closes stdin either way.

`readHiddenLine` restores stdin with `if (wasPaused) input.pause()`, but `isPaused()` returns `flowing === false`, and a fresh `process.stdin` has `flowing === null` — so the `resume()` used for hidden entry is never undone and the still-referenced TTY handle keeps the event loop alive.

The prompt now records whether stdin was actually flowing beforehand (`readableFlowing === true`) and pauses it again whenever it was not. A regression test uses a `process.stdin`-like fake that starts with `readableFlowing = null`.

title: test: make orphaned-lock recovery independent of live PIDs
body:
The orphaned-lock recovery test assumes PID 999999 can never exist. Linux defaults `kernel.pid_max` to 4194304 and thread IDs share the PID space, so `process.kill(999999, 0)` can find a live task — the "orphaned" lock then looks owned and the test fails with `SyncAlreadyRunningError`.

Inject `processIsRunningFn` (an override `withSyncLock` already supports) so the recovery path is exercised deterministically on every machine.

title: Add an ergonomic all-available-history sync mode
body:
## Motivation

`cribble sync` defaults to seven days, while the parser supports up to 365. Syncing every locally available usage day currently requires knowing the internal maximum and running `cribble sync --days 365`.

## Proposed CLI

Add `--all` to foreground show and sync commands:

```sh
cribble --all
cribble sync --all
```

`--all` means scan the maximum locally supported history window, currently 365 days. It should be mutually exclusive with `--days`.

## Compatibility

Keep the existing seven-day default and `--days` validation unchanged. Do not change scheduled background sync behavior.

## Acceptance criteria

- `cribble sync --all` and `cribble --all` scan the current 365-day maximum.
- `--all --days N` fails with a clear error.
- Existing default and explicit `--days` behavior remain unchanged.
- Help and README document the option.
- Regression and CLI smoke tests cover the behavior without uploading data.

title: Support collecting usage from multiple Claude Code profiles
body:
## Problem

I use multiple Claude Code profiles/accounts and want one complete, deduplicated usage view. Cribble currently collects Claude Code usage from only one config directory. Other people who keep personal and work accounts or profiles for the same service have the same problem: switching environments manually can omit usage or repeat totals from Codex and other agents.

## Proposed behavior

Add an opt-in `CRIBBLE_CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIRS` environment variable containing a comma-separated list of absolute Claude config directories. Cribble should:

- validate that entries are absolute existing directories and reject control characters or empty lists;
- deduplicate entries by resolved real path;
- retain one normal ccusage baseline scan for all supported agents;
- scan each additional Claude profile with `--by-agent` and merge only Claude-labeled rows;
- exclude repeated Codex and other-agent rows from additional scans;
- fail closed if any configured profile scan fails; and
- capture the setting in the Linux background service without embedding credentials.

The default single-profile behavior must remain unchanged when the variable is unset. Collection should remain limited to usage metadata and aggregates already handled by Cribble, without reading or publishing conversation content.

## Acceptance criteria

- Multiple Claude Code accounts or profiles contribute their Claude usage once.
- Other agents from additional scans are not duplicated.
- Invalid or failed configured scans abort collection rather than returning partial totals.
- Foreground and Linux background collection honor the same opt-in setting.
- Existing single-profile behavior remains unchanged when the setting is absent.

title: Track privacy-safe Ollama token usage
body:
Closes Birdabo404/Cribble#60.

## Summary

Adds an opt-in, privacy-safe Ollama usage source to Cribble Agent so local models such as Qwen are counted without inventing provider spend.

- reads native Ollama `prompt_eval_count` / `eval_count` counters from a sanitized local ledger
- records local usage with billed provider cost `$0`, while preserving unknown cache/reasoning token classes as unknown
- keeps prompt and response content out of the ledger and upload payload
- uses bounded, descriptor-pinned, owner/mode-validated ledger I/O
- deduplicates the same request across Ollama and existing harness sources while preserving provenance
- preserves event/request identity and timestamps for server-side reconciliation
- uses the same collection path for foreground and scheduled sync

Companion Cribble server PR: https://github.com/Birdabo404/Cribble/pull/73

## Verification

Exact head: `95c65f431b3cc999f7b77ebafa6e82acf4cc26e3`

- `npm test`: 124/124 passed
- cross-source same-request dedup and provenance-union probes passed
- conflict and false-dedup controls passed
- existing permissive ledger repaired to `0600`; symlink/type/ownership/mutation/race failures close safely
- complete-history bundle verified

## Compatibility

title: Pinned ccusage 20.0.20 drops most Claude Code usage (requestless records); bump to ≥ 20.0.28, e.g. merge #31
body:
## Problem

cribble-agent 1.4.x pins `ccusage` to exactly `20.0.20`. Since about early October 2026, Claude Code (seen on 2.1.31x) no longer writes a top-level `requestId` on assistant transcript records. It writes `requestRef` instead. ccusage 20.0.20 drops most of these requestless records, so Cribble badly undercounts Claude Code usage. Sessions started through SDK hosts such as T3 Code (`"entrypoint": "t3-code"`) are hit hardest: on recent days they are almost entirely missing.

ccusage 20.0.28 is the first published release that counts these records correctly. 20.0.21–20.0.26 swing the other way and overcount them (see below), so nothing older than 20.0.28 should be used. Dependabot's bump PRs for ccusage (#25–#30) were each superseded by the next one, so installs are still on 20.0.20. The current one, #31 (20.0.45), is green on every CI job.

## Evidence

One macOS arm64 machine with Claude Code 2.1.316–2.1.318. Days are local time (Europe/Tallinn). "Independent count" sums `message.usage` over assistant records in `~/.claude/projects/**/*.jsonl`, deduplicated by `message.id`.

| Day | ccusage 20.0.20 | ccusage 20.0.48 | Independent count |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2026-11-05 | 3.1M tokens | 3,217.9M | 3,217.9M |
| 2026-11-06 | 1.4M | 2,516.3M | 2,516.3M |
| 2026-11-07 | no row | 711.9M | 711.9M |

- From 2026-09-25 to 2026-11-08, 20.0.20 reported about 53% of the tokens that 20.0.48 reports.
- Across 170 days of local history, 20.0.48 never reported fewer tokens than 20.0.20 for any day. Re-syncing old days with the new version therefore only raises totals.
- The Claude-only totals from 20.0.48 match the independent count to within about 1%.
- Version check on one day (2026-11-05, `ccusage claude daily`): 20.0.20 reports 3.1M. 20.0.21, 20.0.22, 20.0.23, 20.0.24 and 20.0.26 report 5,411.0M, about 1.7× too high. 20.0.28, 20.0.32, 20.0.36, 20.0.37, 20.0.45 and 20.0.48 report 3,217.9M, which matches the independent count. 20.0.25 and 20.0.27 would not install. So #31 (20.0.45) fixes it.
- `npm test` passes with ccusage bumped to 20.0.48 (139 pass, 1 skipped).
- A second Mac showed the same pattern. Its 7-day report went from 1.99B to 9.34B tokens after the bump.

## Suggested fix

Merge #31, or bump `ccusage` to 20.0.48, and publish a patch release. Users then need to re-send older days, because the default background window only covers 7 days.

## Workaround until a release

```sh
cd "$(npm root -g)/cribble-agent" && npm install ccusage@20.0.48 --save-exact
cribble sync --days 70   # re-send older days
```

Running `npm install -g cribble-agent` again brings back the 20.0.20 pin.

## Related observation

The background job runs with `ProcessType=Background` and `LowPriorityIO`. On a large history, the ccusage scan took 153 s under equivalent throttling (`taskpolicy -b -d throttle`), against the default 120 s timeout, and one scheduled sync failed with `ccusage collection timed out after 120000 ms`. Re-running `cribble start` with `CRIBBLE_CCUSAGE_TIMEOUT_MS=300000` works around it. A larger default timeout for background runs might be worth considering.
